name: Jimi Hendrix
reason: Hendrix’s voice is closely tied to Strat-style single-coils and expressive vibrato—these are accessible Strat platforms in that lane.
sourceNote: Curated inspiration from well-documented Strat use; not an official signature match.

name: Jimmy Page
reason: Page’s rock tone is often Les Paul and SG humbuckers; he also leaned on open and DADGAD-style tunings for acoustic textures—these cover both sides.
sourceNote: Inspired by widely reported Les Paul / SG eras and known alternate-tuning acoustic work; not exact stage guitars.

name: Slash
reason: Slash’s sound is strongly linked to Les Paul humbuckers—his Epiphone signature sits first when it fits your budget, with the Studio as a nearby step-in.
sourceNote: Signature SKU called out when in-budget; Studio remains a tone-family alternative.

name: The Edge
reason: The Edge’s chiming, delay-soaked parts often sit on Strat/Tele platforms. Some U2 parts also use drop and altered tunings—these are approachable Fender-family starting points for that lane.
sourceNote: Tone and platform inspiration; delay/FX do much of the signature sound. Catalog has no Explorer—Strat/Tele/Acoustasonic stand in.

name: John Mayer
reason: Mayer’s PRS Silver Sky (core and SE) and Martin OMJM signature lead the list when they fit your price range; Strat and other acoustics fill in the same lane.
sourceNote: Official PRS / Martin signature lines prioritized; other IDs are tone-family backups.

name: Eric Clapton
reason: Clapton’s Martin 000-28EC signature leads on the acoustic side when in budget; Strat platforms cover the electric Blackie-era lane.
sourceNote: Martin EC is the named signature; Strat picks are tone-family, not Fender Custom Shop signatures.

name: Stevie Ray Vaughan
reason: SRV’s blues-rock attack is classic Strat territory—thick pick attack through single-coils.
sourceNote: Inspired by documented Strat preference; our list points to related platforms in-budget.

name: B.B. King
reason: King’s singing lead tone lived in hollow/semi-hollow territory; these are approachable hollow-ish electrics with blues-friendly warmth.
sourceNote: Lucille was a Gibson ES-style guitar; we map to nearby hollow/semi options we stock.

name: Wes Montgomery
reason: Montgomery’s octave-rich jazz voice sits on full or semi-hollow jazz boxes—these are curated jazz-leaning electrics.
sourceNote: Inspired by classic jazz-box association; not a historical exact model claim.

name: Bob Dylan
reason: Dylan’s songwriter sound is dreadnought and flat-top acoustic first—volume and midrange that carry a voice.
sourceNote: Folk/acoustic inspiration across eras; Martin is the heritage end, Yamaha/Seagull more reachable.

name: Joni Mitchell
reason: Mitchell is famous for dozens of alternate tunings and a clear, chord-rich acoustic voice—open, flat-top, and nylon options support that exploratory lane.
sourceNote: Inspired by documented alternate-tuning practice and acoustic focus; not a claim of her exact instruments.

name: John Rzeznik
reason: Rzeznik’s long Taylor relationship puts Taylor Grand Auditoriums first (814ce when budget allows, 314ce as a closer step)—then other acoustics and a Strat for the rock side. Open and altered tunings are part of that songwriter sound.
sourceNote: Taylor artist association / primary stage brand; 814ce is the flagship stand-in (not a named mass-market “Rzeznik” SKU). 314ce is the more reachable Taylor in the same family.

name: Keith Richards
reason: Richards’ rhythm language lives in open-G style tunings and Tele/hollow snap—these are approachable twang and jangle platforms.
sourceNote: Inspired by famous open-G / five-string approach and Tele-adjacent tones; not exact stage guitars.

name: Nick Drake
reason: Drake’s intimate folk fingerstyle leaned on unusual tunings and warm flat-tops—these dreadnought and cedar-top options sit in that quiet, resonant lane.
sourceNote: Inspired by documented alternate tunings and acoustic focus; not museum-exact gear.

name: Ani DiFranco
reason: DiFranco’s percussive, politically charged folk-rock often uses alternate tunings and stage-ready acoustics—clear, responsive tops fit that attack.
sourceNote: Inspired by known alternate-tuning / acoustic-first performance style; not signature models.

name: James Hetfield
reason: Tight, aggressive rhythm metal often leans on high-output humbuckers, fast solid platforms, and drop tunings—these cover that zone.
sourceNote: Tone-family mapping to our catalog; not ESP/Explorer signature replicas.

name: Kirk Hammett
reason: Lead-focused metal with fast necks and high-gain friendly pickups—starter and mid platforms in that direction.
sourceNote: Inspired by shred/metal lead platforms; catalog IDs are accessible relatives.

name: Brad Paisley
reason: Modern country twang and clarity often start with Tele-style snap or Gretsch sparkle.
sourceNote: Inspired by Telecaster association in contemporary country; Gretsch covers flashier country cleans.

name: Johnny Cash
reason: Cash’s sound sits between booming acoustic rhythm and simple electric twang—dreadnoughts and Teles fit that story.
sourceNote: Curated from widely known acoustic/electric associations; not museum-exact gear.
